summary: In the main offices of Meta CorTechs, with windows overlooking downtown, RHINEHEART chides NEO while never glancing his way, his fingers never leaving the keyboard while NEO stares at two window cleaners dragging their squeegees down the glass outside. RHINEHEART accuses NEO of having 'a problem with authority' and believing 'the rules do not apply to you,' then argues that the company's success depends on every employee being 'a part of a whole,' so that 'if a staff member faces an issue, the firm faces an issue.' He pivots and delivers an ultimatum: 'You either report to your desk promptly going forward or you pack your things and find a different position.' After asking 'Do I make myself clear?' NEO replies, 'Yes, Mr. Rhineheart. Perfectly clear.'

what_changes.before: An employee being lectured about his attitude and lateness, treated as someone who thinks he is above the rules
what_changes.after: An employee who has been forced to submit to an explicit ultimatum about his job, outwardly compliant
what_changes.evidence: Either you choose to be at your

what_changes.before: A manager absorbed in his work, addressing NEO without even looking at him
what_changes.after: A manager who has asserted the company's authority and demanded NEO's conformity as 'a part of a whole'
what_changes.evidence: This company is one of the top

event_hint.one_line: RHINEHEART reprimands NEO for his lateness and attitude, ending with an ultimatum that NEO accepts.

uncertain: Whether NEO's 'Perfectly clear' reflects genuine compliance or concealed resentment
Whether RHINEHEART intends to fire NEO immediately if he is late again, or merely to warn him

minds.wants: To force Neo's submission to the company's authority and erase the impression that Neo thinks he is above the rules.
minds.feels: Irritated and mildly contemptuous, but fundamentally uninvested; Neo is a minor administrative friction, not a real threat. He is comfortable lecturing while continuing his actual work.
minds.shows: Cold, controlled authority. He never looks at Neo while typing, delivering the reprimand as background to his own productivity, then turns only to deliver the ultimatum.
minds.basis: He lectures 'without glancing his way, he keeps his fingers flying across the keyboard,' accuses Neo of 'a problem with authority' and believing 'the rules do not apply to you,' frames the company as 'a part of a whole' where 'when one worker struggles, the entire organization struggles,' and ends with the either/or ultimatum. The window-cleaner blocking and the resumed keyboard-clicking show he treats this as routine.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is a petty, arrogant slacker whose lateness stems from a belief in his own specialness.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo's real distance from this world — the sleeplessness and the search Trinity named in sc-013 — has nothing to do with the petty insubordination Rhineheart imagines. Rhineheart is diagnosing a man he has never actually seen.

minds.wants: To endure the lecture with the least possible engagement and get it over with.
minds.feels: Detached and inwardly elsewhere; his attention is on the window cleaners outside, not on the reprimand. The authority being asserted over him does not register as meaningful to who he actually is.
minds.shows: Passive silence during the lecture, then crisp, deferential compliance: 'Yes, Mr. Rhineheart. Perfectly clear.'
minds.basis: He 'stares at two window cleaners' throughout instead of engaging, offers no defense or apology, and answers the ultimatum with flat agreement. His gaze staying on the glass while being told the rules apply to him marks where his mind actually is.

believes_about.belief: That Rhineheart's authority, and this entire workplace hierarchy, is trivial and not worth resisting because it doesn't touch him.
believes_about.wrong_because: The scene's place in the larger event shows this world can in fact reach him — the reprimand is the prelude to police, an interrogation room, and physical modification. His dismissal of this authority is a luxury about to be revoked.

connects_back: Trinity's warning in sc-013 that Neo is 'in danger,' 'they're watching you,' and that he 'hardly sleeps' and lives alone — framing his lateness and detachment as symptoms of a search, not the petty rebellion Rhineheart assumes.
The 9:15 A.M. alarm and Neo's 'Shitshitshit' in sc-014, which is the immediate cause of the lateness Rhineheart is punishing.
The downtown skyscraper of Meta CorTechs established in sc-015, the same windows the cleaners are on in this scene.
sets_up: The ultimatum's stakes make Neo's subsequent inability to conform legible — he will not become the compliant employee Rhineheart demands, which drives him toward the phone, the escape attempt, and the capture in ev-003.
Neo's hollow, unresisting 'Perfectly clear' prefigures how he will perform compliance under far greater pressure from Agent Smith in ev-003 before ultimately refusing.

Rhineheart's belief that Neo merely has 'a problem with authority' sets up the larger mistake of the system about Neo — that he is a small problem to be corrected rather than 'The One' revealed in ev-004.
dramatic_function: It dramatizes the ordinary world's attempt to discipline Neo into conformity and establishes how little that authority actually reaches him — the reprimand reads as petty bureaucracy against a man already being pulled toward something vast, sharpening the irony that this 'special' accusation is both trivially wrong and, in a way Rhineheart cannot imagine, about to become true.
